chapters.title: The House of Flowers
chapters.intro: Day One. Spanish in order of encounter.
vocabulary: Can ask; misses most of the answer
chapters.notes:
**What I know:** Evelyn used to teach literature. Isabel's family has owned this lovely hotel for years. The foundation on the flyer is familiar from the office.

**What I wonder:** Whether Nate's definition of “a little spicy” will improve. Must remember the beach bar.

chapters.title: A Familiar Face
chapters.intro: Days Two and Three. Spanish in order of encounter.
evidence: I heard Tomás ask this, but I don't know the meaning yet.
Tomás said this while talking to Isabel. I didn't catch the meaning.
chapters.notes:
**What I know:** Clara is Evelyn's daughter. Mariana has a lovely hummingbird tattoo she doesn't want her parents to know about. Isabel took a small silver key from Tomás.

**What I wonder:** Whether Clara is enjoying her visit as much as she'd hoped. Also, why does that bakery have to be so far from our hotel?

chapters.title: Things Best Left Alone
chapters.intro: Wednesday, Day Four. Spanish in order of encounter.
vocabulary: Tomás explains the word used earlier when he was talking to Isabel.
chapters.notes:
**What I know:** Graham helped Clara's family when her father died. Charles intends to send a statement to a solicitor tomorrow. Evelyn wanted them to do something together instead. Lucía has written about New Horizons before.

**What I wonder:** What made Clara so unhappy at the reception? I hope she and Evelyn manage to talk. Nate and I have a new beach to explore tomorrow.

chapters.title: A Change of Plans
chapters.intro: Thursday, Day Five. Spanish in order of encounter.
vocabulary: Understands Isabel's gesture; meaning confirmed by context
chapters.notes:
**What I know:** Charles Whitmore died this morning. Diego says he witnessed a push and heard Charles say, “You promised me she would never have to read it.” He could not identify the other person. Diego saw Charles with the repaired leather case earlier. He told the police. I told Inspector Salazar what I heard yesterday and what Graham said about intending to meet Charles today but not seeing him.

**What I wonder:** Who was Charles speaking about? Was his disagreement with Evelyn connected to what happened? I hope Diego has someone to talk to.

chapters.title: Beyond the Hotel
chapters.intro: Friday, Day Six. Spanish in order of encounter.
vocabulary: Understands after the price is written down
Dos vasos de agua, por favor
I don't want to talk about that
Recognizes part; Mariana supplies full meaning
chapters.notes:
**What I know:** The foundation's public display shows a woman with Mariana's tattoo and face. It claims her birthmark was entirely cleared six months ago. Mariana still has a visible mark. She did not want to discuss the photograph. Graham had a leather case with a repaired handle like the one Charles carried.

**What I wonder:** Is there an innocent explanation for the photograph? Lucía may know something about the foundation's earlier publicity. I will not press Mariana.

chapters.title: An Old Acquaintance
chapters.intro: Saturday, Day Seven. Spanish in order of encounter.
vocabulary: Understands retrospectively after Tomás explains the cupboard
evidence: Tomás asked Isabel something about the papers. I recognized *dónde*.
chapters.notes:
**What I know:** Lucía obtained the earlier original photograph and showed me that the two images on the foundation display come from the same picture. The supposed after image was altered. This does not establish whether Mariana received treatment. Rosa used the silver key for the event-supplies cupboard. Evelyn seems to regret something about the past.

**What I wonder:** Who decided to use the altered photograph, and why? Does the foundation's dishonesty have anything to do with Charles's death, or are these separate matters?

vocabulary: Could you repeat that more slowly, please?
Also **¿Pica mucho?** — Is it very spicy?
Una mesa para dos, por favor.
Also **¿Cuánto es?** — How much is it? Useful for asking the total at checkout.
travelers.tip: Tip: Learn nouns with their articles. **El hotel** means “the hotel”; **la llave** means “the key.” For grammar explanations, examples, and pronunciation practice, use the companion app.
